dedupe_keys.name: simulated outage of the ix br sao paulo internet exchange point isoc pulse fellowship 2026

description: This blog post summarises a Pulse fellowship study that mapped the peering topology of the IX.br Sao Paulo Internet exchange point by active probing and simulated the effect of the exchange going down on connected networks. The probing found about 847,000 links, 795 times as many as traceroutes reveal, yet only about 14.45 percent of more than five million possible links, showing limited visibility. The simulation found that 10 percent of links have no shorter alternative path and about 15 percent could see longer paths; DE-CIX Sao Paulo and Equinix Sao Paulo share 13,110 links with IX.br, so a failure cascades to them, and under full load the diverted traffic could exceed their link capacity by more than 10 times on average and over 100 times in some cases. Producer: Nishant Acharya (UC Davis) for the Internet Society Pulse programme. Coverage: one exchange in Sao Paulo, Brazil, with two neighbours. Access: a free public blog post with figures; the data and methodology are available by contacting the author. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: a short summary, not a peer-reviewed paper, with figures showing only 30 percent of the discovered topology. Simulation uses: the method shows how to test IXP failure and traffic diversion in resilience and cascading-failure models. Related records: the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database), PeeringDB (data-peeringdb) and the PEERING testbed (case_study-peering-bgp-testbed).
